newsitem.title: TURKEY: Germany's Kinkel meets Turk human rights leaders.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kinkel meets Turk human rights leaders.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel expressed support for the work of Turkey's embattled human rights activists at a closed-door meeting on Thursday, participants said.
"He said he knows that (non-governmental organisations) NGOs are in a difficult situation in Turkey and said he supported our work," said Human Rights Association chairman Akin Birdal.

Birdal was one of four human rights workers who met Kinkel over breakfast at a five-star hotel. "He mentioned the human rights and Kurdish problems and the fact that they have not been solved," Birdal told Reuters.

Kinkel, on a two-day official visit, said on Wednesday that Turkey belongs in Europe but that its poor human rights record and its fight with Kurdish separatist rebels were two obstacles in the way of Ankara joining the European Union.
Another participant in the meeting said the Kinkel delegation showed an interest in the condition of Turkish women, many of whom feel under pressure from the growing Islamist movement.

The European Parliament has blocked hundreds of millions of dollars in EU aid to Turkey because of its human rights performance. Human rights activists are often put on trial for their work and accused of collaboration with Kurdish rebels.
